messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: Latency SLO breaches detected - p95/p99 elevated for streaming endpoints in region us-west-2. Auto-escalation to on-call. Root thread 3300004321

alex m: seeing the bot - I'm oncall. what's the scope? p95/p99 numbers?

priya r: p95 jumped from ~220ms -> ~1.3s over last 10m, p99 from ~620ms -> 9-12s. Streaming stalls reported by clients: a lot of half-second gaps then long stalls. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streaming/kv-pressure?orgId=1

cheng li: logs show repeated kv-cache evictions across shards 4-7, eviction rate spike at 2026-03-15T02:12Z. IFF: eviction bursts correlate with high prefill rates for long-context requests. Disk paging I/O also bumped on hosts serving those shards (/dev/nvme2n1).

samir: confirmed: disk iowait climbs from ~2% to 38% during eviction spikes. When eviction starts, tail latency for streaming tokens jumps -> client timeouts.

brynn: customer support reports 3 customers saw request timeouts >30s; some callouts in #support. Impacted routes: /v1/stream/generate (model: gpt-open-3-std) and /v1/chat/stream.

alex m: triage plan: 1) reduce ongoing customer impact 2) stabilize tails 3) root cause. Immediate mitigations?

priya r: short-term mitigations I can toggle now: - reduce_prefill=true gate to limit prefill worker spawn - lower batch_size for streaming to avoid big KV inserts - escalate cache TTL to reduce churn (bump from 60s -> 300s for high-frequency keys)

cheng li: prefill vs decode imbalance note: prefill threads are producing many KV entries for long-context prompts that rarely hit again; decode path reads are heavier but post-eviction decode falls back to disk which stalls. If we throttle prefill we reduce churn and evictions.

samir: we can also roll a small scale-up of cache nodes for shards 4-7. Ops can spin new cache pods with higher mem and bring them into the ring. But that is ~8-12m.

ops-bot: Runbooks available: /runbooks/kv-cache-eviction.md. Suggested commands below.

priya r: immediate actions I'm doing now (ETA minutes): 1) flip feature gate reduce_prefill -> true (admin API) 2) set eviction_threshold to 0.85 from 0.75 for shards 4-7 3) increase high-frequency TTL to 300s 4) temporarily disable streaming chunking to force smaller writes.

alex m: please paste exact admin commands before you run. I will notify customers and update severity.

priya r: running now:

```bash
# flip prefill gate
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood/api/flags" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"flag":"reduce_prefill","value":true}'

# bump eviction threshold for shards
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood/api/cache/shard/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"shards":[4,5,6,7],"eviction_threshold":0.85}'

# increase TTL for hf keys
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood/api/cache/ttl" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"pattern":"hf_*","ttl":300}'
```

priya r: done. logs show prefill worker starts dropping by ~60% within 30s. Eviction rate trending down.

cheng li: good. monitor decode queue length. If decode queue grows we might need to throttle incoming traffic or divert to fallback model.

samir: I'll start provisioning two cache-highmem pods for shards 4/5. ETA ~9m. Command: kubectl -n caching scale statefulset/cache-shard-4 --replicas=3 (already at 1) and similar for shard-5. Ops will monitor disk iowait.

brynn: support: notif going out to impacted customers now: "We're investigating elevated latency on streaming endpoints and applying mitigations. No data loss. We'll follow up with timeline."

alex m: severity set to P2. adding on-call handoff notes: Priya take initial mitigation lead, Cheng you take follow-up root cause and postmortem, Samir coordinate infra scaling, Brynn handle customer comms. I'll stay on until stabilization then handoff to Cheng in 30m.

priya r: quick note: disabling streaming chunking had to be reverted — caused transient regen of large prefills. reverted. current stable: reduce_prefill true + TTL bump + eviction_threshold bump.

ops-bot: Alert: cache_shard_4_iowait dropped from 38% -> 6% after interventions. eviction_rate down 72%.

cheng li: seeing p99 drop to 2.1s and p95 ~420ms in us-west-2 at 02:38Z. still above target but much improved. streaming stalls much lower.

samir: cache pod scale completed for shards 4/5. memory headroom increased. disk iowait steady.

brynn: support update sent to customers with ETA 2h for full stabilization and a post-incident follow-up. customers asked for root cause; we'll share after postmortem.

alex m: good progress. remaining tasks: - run cache compaction for fragmented shards - audit prefill logs to identify long-context patterns - add alert for prefill:decode imbalance (metric: prefill_rate/decode_rate > 2x) - decide on permanent config changes (TTL/eviction policy).

cheng li: I'll run compaction command on shards 4-7 during low traffic window (scheduled 03:10Z) and collect samples of keys causing churn. Also will instrument a histogram for prefill KV sizes.

priya r: handoff: I'm handing to Cheng in 25m. If anything spikes >p99 8s, page SRE escalation. Alex, will you stay as escalation lead?

alex m: staying until Cheng confirms post-compact metrics. thanks team.

incident-bot: UPDATE: Incident severity P2 -> Monitoring. p95/p99 trending down. Postmortem requested within 72h.

cheng li: postmortem TODOs I'll own: timeline, root cause (prefill-heavy workload + small cache mem + fragmentation + eviction-triggered disk paging), mitigations applied, follow-ups (long-term: smarter prefill sampling, compaction daemon, per-customer prefill caps, add safeguard to auto-throttle prefill when eviction_rate > X).

samir: ops follow-ups: ensure autoscaling policy for cache shards has burst capacity, add runbook step to temporarily divert traffic to fallback model variant when decode queue > Y.

brynn: PRD notes: customer comms template + list of impacted tenants saved to /docs/incidents/3300004321/comm-log.md

alex m: closing note: great quick work. we'll keep this thread for postmortem comments. If anyone sees p99 >6s re-open and tag @alex m and @cheng li. :thumbsup:
